organization: Region Roots Local Farm and Food Hub
evidence_of_produce_aggregation: Aggregates produce from multiple NW Indiana farms across 7 counties (Lake, Porter, LaPorte, Newton, Jasper, Starke, Pulaski); operates as a nonprofit local food hub since 2021
evidence_of_institutional_buyers: Awarded Local Food for Schools grant from Indiana Dept of Health; explicit farm-to-school program
pain_hypothesis: Multi-farm aggregation with manual order/inventory coordination across 7 counties; likely has lot tracking and traceability gaps that increase with each new institutional buyer
notes: SEGMENT: produce_hub. Parent: NWI Food Council. Mission-driven nonprofit — pricing sensitivity higher, but pilot-friendly because they want to professionalize ops.

evidence_of_produce_aggregation: Farmer-owned online farmers cooperative aggregating from multiple Indiana farms; pickup locations in 6 Indiana cities; established 2013
evidence_of_institutional_buyers: Wholesale section indicates institutional buyer involvement though not detailed publicly
pain_hypothesis: Cooperative model with farmer-owners means manual data entry across multiple pickup locations; wholesale orders likely tracked in spreadsheets
notes: SEGMENT: produce_hub. Coordinator email: coordinator@hoosierharvestmarket.com. Office at Hancock County Extension Office, 802 Apple St, Greenfield IN 46140.

evidence_of_produce_aggregation: USDA AMS-grant-funded food hub at Kalamazoo Valley CC; aggregates from SW Michigan farms; offers wash/peel/chop/freeze services
evidence_of_institutional_buyers: Serves regional institutional markets — explicit on their site
pain_hypothesis: Light processing services + aggregation creates lot tracking and yield-loss visibility gaps; community college affiliation means complex procurement and reporting requirements
notes: SEGMENT: produce_hub. Address: 224 E Crosstown Pkwy, Kalamazoo MI 49001. Note: institutional affiliation (community college) may mean longer decision cycle. Light processing also makes this a hybrid produce_hub/fresh_cut prospect.

evidence_of_produce_aggregation: Founded 2017 as nonprofit; aggregates from Northeast Ohio farmers and makers; offers centralized ordering, cold storage, logistics
evidence_of_institutional_buyers: Explicitly serves 'schools, food banks, retailers, and distributors across Ohio and surrounding states'
pain_hypothesis: Centralized ordering + cold storage + invoicing + logistics — exactly the operational stack where waste, near-expiry, and traceability data live in disconnected spreadsheets
notes: SEGMENT: produce_hub. Cleveland address (4540 Commerce Ave, 44103) despite Oberlin name. Strong fit. Phone has 617 (Boston) area code — verify before calling.

evidence_of_produce_aggregation: Connects Flint-area farmers with buyers; operates processing kitchen for chopping and cooking
evidence_of_institutional_buyers: Mentioned by Michigan Food Hub Network as part of regional aggregation/distribution
pain_hypothesis: Processing kitchen + aggregation in a community-focused Michigan hub — likely manual order taking, manual inventory across farm-buyer match-making
notes: SEGMENT: produce_hub. Contact info needs to be pulled from their site. Community/social-impact focus — pricing sensitivity expected.

evidence_of_produce_aggregation: Listed as a community-focused food hub in West Michigan / Grand Rapids region; aggregator for regional farms
evidence_of_institutional_buyers: Inferred from Michigan Food Hub Network membership; not explicitly verified for institutional sales
pain_hypothesis: Suspected aggregator with multi-farm coordination needs; verification needed before outreach
notes: SEGMENT: produce_hub. NEEDS VERIFICATION. Listed by Taste the Local Difference but website not fully verified for current activity. Drop in priority order until validated.

evidence_of_produce_aggregation: Massachusetts oyster grower since 2001; operates own oyster farms PLUS carries over 100 oyster varieties from Atlantic and Pacific; clearly aggregates from multiple sources
evidence_of_institutional_buyers: Serves distributors, restaurants, retailers, corporate groups
pain_hypothesis: Mixing own-farm production with 100+ sourced varieties means lot tracking and shelf-life management across many supplier inputs — classic perishable ATP and waste exposure
notes: SEGMENT: seafood. Recent activity through Nov 2025. Strong product mix + supplier diversity. Contact via website /contact form.

evidence_of_produce_aggregation: Cape Cod-based wholesale; sources from local fishing families and small boat fisheries; HACCP, FDA, and MRAG Americas certified
evidence_of_institutional_buyers: Restaurants and commercial buyers nationwide — chefs around the country
pain_hypothesis: Aggregates from multiple small boat fisheries; lot codes per boat; perishable inventory management across multiple species (oysters, clams, lobsters, scallops). FDA + HACCP certified means structured but probably paperwork-heavy
notes: SEGMENT: seafood. Address: 137 Holmes Road, Eastham MA 02642. Very strong fit for traceability + lot tracking diagnostic angle.

evidence_of_produce_aggregation: Small independent oyster farm in Chatham MA producing own oysters; occasionally sources from other local oyster producers
evidence_of_institutional_buyers: Sells direct to chefs and wholesale buyers
pain_hypothesis: Smaller farm but still has lot/harvest tag pain plus FDA/state shellfish reporting; growth-blocked-by-paperwork pattern from Reddit signal applies
notes: SEGMENT: seafood. Smaller scale = may not yet have budget for paid pilot. Worth a discovery call regardless to gather operator language.

evidence_of_produce_aggregation: Aggregates from Ward Oyster Co. (sister company with own hatchery) plus wild-caught sources; 3.5 million oysters per year
evidence_of_institutional_buyers: Wholesale to distributors and restaurants; retail facility; nationwide online delivery
pain_hypothesis: Multi-source aggregation (own hatchery + wild + sister company) + multi-channel (wholesale, retail, online) means lot tracking and inventory allocation across channels is operationally complex
notes: SEGMENT: seafood. Ware Neck VA 23178. Larger seafood operator — possible Path C signal. Family business since 1995.

evidence_of_produce_aggregation: Fourth-generation family wholesale produce distributor since 1939; 2 facilities (Ravenna + Norwalk OH); operates in-house produce processor Christine's Cuts
evidence_of_institutional_buyers: Distributes 6 days a week to restaurants, hotels, country clubs, schools, and institutions in OH, central PA, and northern WV
pain_hypothesis: 81-year family operation with multi-product, multi-location, schools-and-institutions mix — exactly the data complexity HarvestMind diagnoses
notes: SEGMENT: food_bev_distributor. Address: 7176 State Route 88, Ravenna OH 44266. Hybrid distributor + in-house fresh-cut (Christine's Cuts). Best single fit across the list.

evidence_of_produce_aggregation: Family-owned since 1989 in Columbus OH; both bulk and fresh-cut produce; multi-state distribution
evidence_of_institutional_buyers: Explicit school service customer segment; serves food service, manufacturing, school service, government, retail in OH, MI, PA, IL, IN, MO, WI, NJ, KY, TN, WV
pain_hypothesis: Multi-state distribution + fresh-cut + bulk + government/school programs = high data complexity and high traceability stakes (especially for school nutrition compliance)
notes: SEGMENT: food_bev_distributor. Possibly upper end of size range for early pilot (may have existing ERP). Worth a discovery call to test Path C signal.

evidence_of_produce_aggregation: Family/woman-owned (WBENC certified); 125,000 sq ft across Chicago and Kenosha facilities; SQF-certified
evidence_of_institutional_buyers: Serves restaurants, schools, hospitals, retail, corporate, wholesale across IL, WI, IN, MI
pain_hypothesis: Multi-segment buyers (schools, hospitals, restaurants, corporate) + multi-state means strong fulfillment-rate and lot-tracking diagnostic angle; SQF certification implies structured records but reconciliation is still manual
notes: SEGMENT: food_bev_distributor. Chicago: 3100 W. 36th Street; Kenosha: 6950 51st Street. Family-and-woman-owned creates strong advisor recruiting angle.

evidence_of_produce_aggregation: Family-owned wholesale food distributor since 1960; delivers fresh and frozen products across Ohio
evidence_of_institutional_buyers: Restaurants, schools, hospitals, delis, pizza shops across Ohio
pain_hypothesis: 60+ year family business handling fresh and frozen across diverse institutional buyer types — likely manual inventory + paper-trail tracking
notes: SEGMENT: food_bev_distributor. Contact info needs further research — website should have it.

evidence_of_produce_aggregation: Family-owned fresh-cut fruit and vegetable processor and distributor; cut and delivered within 24 hours
evidence_of_institutional_buyers: Premier provider to Michigan, Indiana, Ohio grocery stores
pain_hypothesis: 24-hour cut-to-deliver window means extreme near-expiry exposure; tray-size SKU variety amplifies inventory complexity
notes: SEGMENT: fresh_cut. Family-owned. Site returns 403 on About page — recommend phone/LinkedIn outreach to surface contact.

evidence_of_produce_aggregation: Western Pennsylvania's premier fresh food distributor for 135 years; operates fresh-cut under Garden Cut banner; services Ohio, Western PA, West Virginia
evidence_of_institutional_buyers: Tri-state region (OH, W. PA, WV) — restaurants and retail
pain_hypothesis: Long-established operation now part of FreshEdge group; fresh-cut + distribution under one roof with multi-state operations and complex SKU mix
notes: SEGMENT: fresh_cut. NOW PART OF FRESHEDGE GROUP — independent decision authority unclear. Likely already has ERP. Lower priority but worth one discovery call to test Path C.

evidence_of_produce_aggregation: Michigan-based fresh-cut produce processor; positions as 'Chef-driven, cut to order' for restaurants and businesses across the Midwest
evidence_of_institutional_buyers: Restaurants and foodservice businesses across the Midwest
pain_hypothesis: Cut-to-order means short shelf life and high near-expiry risk on day-to-day inventory; chef-driven SKUs increase variability
notes: SEGMENT: fresh_cut. Smaller independent. Strong segment fit. Recommend deeper site research to surface contact.

notes: SEGMENT: institutional. Acquired Local Foods Chicago. Regional team page available for contacts. Single most institutional-focused entity on the list.

evidence_of_produce_aggregation: Organic and regenerative farm + aggregator in Matteson IL (south Chicago suburbs); aggregates from regional farmers
evidence_of_institutional_buyers: USDA contracts; institutional buyers
pain_hypothesis: Smaller aggregator-and-farm combo with mixed retail/wholesale/USDA channels — manual order routing and inventory likely
notes: SEGMENT: institutional. Small operator. May not yet be at scale for a paid pilot — worth a discovery call to gather operator language and surface near-term scaling pain.

evidence_of_institutional_buyers: Schools (explicitly Madison Metropolitan School District); broader farm-to-school work
